decisions.decision: Renderer is a digest-pinned Docker image (ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli 11.17.0@sha256:a6fb05...), NOT pnpm dlx
decisions.rationale: Puppeteer renders text with the host's fonts, which npm cannot pin, so the drift check would report noise on any other machine. pnpm dlx form kept in the script header as a documented non-reproducible fallback.

decisions.decision: Match criterion = exact width at manifest scale + 2% height tolerance; colour mode reported not gated
decisions.rationale: Measured: widths reproduce to the pixel, heights drift in opposite directions across diagrams, ruling out a scale artefact. mmdc cannot force RGB and the script stays stdlib-only.

decisions.decision: Seven pre-existing drifted PNGs left untouched, drift filed as a todo
decisions.rationale: They are the evidence for the renderer-drift finding; silently re-rendering would erase it.

context_notes: Session was one full quick-task cycle (plan -> isolated executor -> my own verification -> user review -> fix round -> merge -> deploy) plus a forensics observation. main = 5b3142d, pushed, deployed green. Probes still running, expire ~04:47Z 2026-09-06: local ~/dev/kanban-net-forensics/probe.csv (819 rows, 1 failure), VM /var/tmp/net-forensics/samples.csv (903 rows). The key forensic lesson: the VM passive_opens counter barely moves while hundreds of probes succeed, because Docker DNAT terminates them in caddy's network namespace — the paired-probe design cannot deliver the direct proof it was built for. Kill probes by PID from pgrep -af, never pkill -f (the pattern matches the SSH command itself).
